# A row-selecting grid starts no cell edit from the keyboard

## Context

Leaf of #18762. `RowModel` is the grid's **default** selection model (`learn/guides/datahandling/Grids.md`, "Selection Models"). With `cellEditing: true` and that default, a keyboard user cannot start an edit at all, and after a pointer-started edit the arrow keys lose their place. Measured in real Chromium (Playwright e2e rig, dev@7db03e862c), not derived.

## The Problem

Fixture `test/playwright/component/apps/grid-cell-editing`, grid `#grid-cell-editing-pooled`, `view.selectionModel` switched to `RowModel` at runtime:

| Step | Editors | Selected rows |
|---|---|---|
| click record 3's `c3` | 0 | record 3 |
| Enter | **0** | record 3 |
| F2 | **0** | record 3 |
| ArrowDown, then Enter | **0** | record 4 |
| double-click record 3's `c3` (control) | 1 | **none** — the two clicks toggled the row on and off |
| type, Enter (commit) | 0 | **none**, focus on the View |
| ArrowDown | 0 | **record 2** — the arrows restart from the store's first record |

So under the default model the feature is pointer-only (WCAG 2.1.1), and a committed edit on row 250 sends the next ArrowDown to row 2.

The public example hides this: `examples/grid/cellEditing` offers only the four cell-selecting models. The guide says "Enter or F2 edits the selected cell" and never names the precondition.

Source authority: D#17832's interaction convergence — "double-click, F2 and Enter activate an editable **active target**" and "Selection is neither necessary nor sufficient across Row/Cell selection models". The shipped keyboard path takes its target from the cell selection alone.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/grid/plugin/CellEditing.mjs#editSelectedCell` (`:178–184`) reads `view.selectedCells[0]`; `grid.View#selectedCells` (`src/grid/View.mjs:137`) returns `[]` for a model without `selectsCells`. Enter and F2 on the View both route there.
- `#onEnterKey` (`:388–404`) re-selects the edited cell after a commit only when `selectionModel.selectsCells`; a row-only model gets no anchor back.
- `src/selection/grid/RowModel.mjs:75`: with no selected row the nav keys start from `store.getAt(0)`.
- A row's selection toggles per click, so a double-click deselects the row it edits (`RowModel#onRowClick`).
- The born-suspended start (`startEdit(record, dataField, true)` + `view.scrollByRows` / `scrollByColumns`, the Tab path in `#onTabKey`) already embodies an edit whose cell is outside the mounted window.

## The Fix

In `src/grid/plugin/CellEditing.mjs`:

1. The keyboard target follows the selection: a selected cell wins (unchanged). With a selected row and no selected cell → that row's record, in the column of the grid's last edit while that column is still editable, else the record's first editable column in arrow-walk order. A target out of sight is scrolled into it through the Tab path (one helper, `editInSight`, for both).
2. A model that selects rows follows the edit by its row: `startEdit` selects the edited record's row when it is not selected, so every end (Enter, Escape, Tab past either end) leaves it selected.

**Scope amendment (2026-09-19, measured while implementing):** rule 2 was first scoped to models that select rows and *no* cells. A probe on the public example under "Cell & Row" falsified that guard: today Tab into the next record selects the cell and leaves **no** row selected, and a double-click edit ended by Escape leaves nothing selected; with the rule applied to every row-selecting model the cell's row follows the Tab and stays as the anchor after Escape, where Enter edits it again. The guard is gone, and two arms on the public example pin it.

New spec `test/playwright/e2e/grid/CellEditingRowModel.spec.mjs` (sibling of the six `CellEditing*.spec.mjs`); the fixture's `gridDriver.mjs` gains the runtime model switch, so no existing witness's fixture default changes. The guide's "Starting an Edit" names the rule per model family.

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Enter / F2 on `grid.View` with `cellEditing` | D#17832 "active target"; `CellEditing#editSelectedCell` | a selected row and no selected cell: edits that row's record (last-edit column, else first editable), scrolled into sight | neither a cell nor a row selected: starts nothing | Grids guide, "Starting an Edit" | e2e arms, red on dev |
| an edit under a row-selecting model (`RowModel`, `CellRowModel`, `CellColumnRowModel`) | `CellEditing#onEnterKey` re-select for cell models | the edited record's row is selected from the start of the edit, and `grid.View` fires `select` for it | — | "Ending an Edit" | e2e arms: ArrowDown after a commit selects the next record; "Cell & Row" on the public example |

## Decision Record impact

none (aligned with D#17832's active-target principle).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Under `RowModel`, Enter and F2 on a selected row each start an edit on that record; with no selected row nothing starts and no error is logged.
- [ ] The column is the last edit's while still editable, else the record's first editable one; a target outside the mounted column window is scrolled into sight and embodied, focused.
- [ ] After Enter, Escape, and a Tab that ends the edit at an end of the store (witnessed: Shift+Tab before the first cell) under `RowModel`, the edited record's row is selected, and ArrowDown selects the next record — also for an edit started by double-click.
- [ ] Under a model that selects cells and rows, Tab into the next record selects its cell and its row, and a double-click edit ended by Escape keeps its row selected.
- [ ] The existing grid e2e and component arms stay green.
- [ ] The new arms are red on dev and mutation-pinned; `--repeat-each=20` clean.
- [ ] The Grids guide states the keyboard rule, with every behavioural claim mapped to an arm.

## Out of Scope

- Changing `RowModel`'s click-toggle itself (a double-click deselecting the row it lands on).
- Type-to-replace activation (D#17832 keeps it outside the first epic).
- Adding `RowModel` to the public example's radio group.

## Avoided Traps

- Forcing a cell-selecting model whenever `cellEditing` is on: it overrides an app's selection contract to fix an activation path.
- Documenting the precondition only: the default configuration would stay keyboard-inaccessible.
